title: With Dave Bartholomew, Joe Liggins and the California trip
summary: He worked with Bartholomew in 1947-48, left with Joe Liggins for California, returned, and the band recorded Fats Domino at the J&M studio.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: Have you traveled around the country very much?

Or... Well, uh... I'm 51. Right after... Right after... recording around town... No, I think it was right after... After I came from California. Because I was living in this house. I worked with Dave Martholomeo at... 48... 47 and 48, I think. Mm-hmm.
I left him... And... To go with Joe Liggins. I left town with Joe Liggins. Oh, yeah. And I wound up in California. So... Yeah.
Were you out in California very long?
I stayed there about three months.
Well, you had a job that day or working that day with him? I was working with him.
Were you on that honey dripper? And I left California to come back on the road with him. Were you on that honey dripper record by any chance?
That was his big hit, wasn't it?
That's the thing that made him popular.

Well, that was before... Before your time. Mm-hmm. Mm-hmm. And I came back to town and worked with Dave Martholomeo. And that's when the band recorded Fast Domino. Yeah. The band recorded Fast Domino, I think I was here. Maybe a year and a half. Back a year and a half after, you know, when we recorded Fast Domino.
We had been scuffling, trying to make records before that to get something to go, you know.
Where were most of those Fast records made today? Yeah. Is that the old J&M studio?
The old J&M studio moved on Governor Nichols.
Were some of them made over on Rampart Street in those days? That's right.
